about: scripts/examples mutants of the ts leg (X-rpc1) and the examples runner's check/native agreement guard (EV6). The ts example killers run under -tags ts, which needs Bun and a warmed Bun cache: go run ./scripts/examples -tags ts limiter.

mutants.name: cu5-domain-origin-lost
mutants.rule: The worked provider preserves the refused origin in its domain failure.

mutants.name: cu6-save-origin-lost
mutants.rule: The worked provider's Save preserves the refused origin in its domain failure.

mutants.name: e3b-law-missing
mutants.rule: The failure coverage law refuses a missing status.

mutants.name: e3b-law-repeat
mutants.rule: The failure coverage law refuses repeated statuses.

mutants.name: e3-direct-empty
mutants.rule: Jobs rejects an empty draft even when called directly, without DraftOf's HTTP validation.

mutants.name: e3-route-missing
mutants.rule: RoutesCoverEndpoints refuses a table missing an endpoint.

mutants.name: e3-route-repeat
mutants.to:
http.Route{Value: endpoint.ShowJob, Method: "GET", Path: "/jobs/:id", Status: 200},
	http.Route{Value: endpoint.ShowJob, Method: "GET", Path: "/jobs/:id", Status: 200},
mutants.rule: RoutesCoverEndpoints refuses a repeated endpoint even when Match returns the same response.

mutants.name: cu1-route-targets-lost
mutants.rule: The worked command maps every repeated target into the domain command, in order.

mutants.name: ts-skip
mutants.rule: A ts program the leg cannot run fails; it never passes with its cases unrun.

mutants.name: ts-layout
mutants.rule: A ts/ folder and the tag ts go together.

mutants.name: ts-package
mutants.rule: A case's copy has its own package.json, so ergo-ts/bun resolves to the installed package.

mutants.name: ts-path
mutants.rule: The checkout's ergo is first on PATH for the content mapper.

mutants.name: r3b-hold-release
mutants.rule: A Hold's release runs on every exit, a stop of its caller included: a client that hangs up on the gateway stops the Ergo Hold, and its release is seen.

mutants.name: r3b-hold-wake
mutants.rule: An Advance wakes every waiting Hold, so a Hold the clock lets through is granted.

mutants.name: x2-same-origin
mutants.rule: One listener serves the RPC mount beside the page's files: /rpc reaches rpc.Answer, not http.Files.

mutants.name: x2-cancel-ended
mutants.rule: A job that has ended stays ended: a cancel of it is rejected (AlreadyDone with its state), never a second end.

mutants.name: cu3-starter-git-ignored
mutants.rule: --git makes the plan a repository, so its files end with .gitignore.

mutants.name: cu3-starter-feature-file-swapped
mutants.rule: Each feature makes its own file.

mutants.name: gcoom-examples-text-only
mutants.rule: A capped example's span-queue allocation fault is memory, not a crash.

mutants.name: examples-ignore-evaluation
mutants.from: if evaluation != nil && err == nil && o.overCap() == "" && !o.timedOut {
mutants.to: if false && evaluation != nil && err == nil && o.overCap() == "" && !o.timedOut {
mutants.rule: Every example compares each check-time verdict and its evidence with the native test verdict, not just exit codes.

mutants.name: gateex-programs-serial
mutants.rule: The runner runs -jobs programs at once, not one at a time.

mutants.name: gateex-output-by-completion
mutants.rule: Each program's lines print in selection order, whatever order the programs end in.

mutants.name: ex-ledger-unchecked
mutants.from: if now, err := os.ReadFile(ledger); err == nil && bytes.Equal(now, kept) {
mutants.to: if now, err := os.ReadFile(ledger); true || err == nil && bytes.Equal(now, kept) {
mutants.rule: A checked-in ergo.laws that the program's ergo test changes fails the ledger leg.

mutants.name: ex-ledger-not-restored
mutants.from: if err := os.WriteFile(ledger, kept, 0o644); err != nil {
mutants.rule: The runner puts a checked-in ergo.laws back as it was: a run leaves the tree unchanged.

mutants.name: ert-explore-leg-case-timeout
mutants.rule: An explore search ends by itself; only -test-timeout, the safety net for a hung one, stops it, never a case's -timeout (batch 18: a healthy search failed 30 s at load 50).

mutants.name: ert-case-timeout-fixed
mutants.rule: A case is stopped only when it hangs: -timeout's default is the test legs' safety net, never a time limit that fails a slow case under load (AGENTS.md, Tests).

mutants.name: ert-budget-wall-time
mutants.rule: The default budget charges a case's CPU time, never its wall time: the host's load does not fail a healthy case (owner, 2026-11-12).

mutants.name: one-module-per-package
mutants.rule: The test leg of a program of packages is one ergo test DIR/..., one check of the module and one test binary, not one per package.

mutants.name: one-module-ignores-evaluation
mutants.rule: One ergo test of a program of packages still compares each package's check-time verdicts with its part of the native report.

mutants.name: one-module-ignores-skips
mutants.to: if skips := unexpectedSkips(section, p.dir); false && len(skips) > 0 {
mutants.rule: One ergo test of a program of packages fails a package whose part of the report holds a skip that expected-skips does not list (fs4).

mutants.name: one-module-any-packages
mutants.rule: A run that tested other packages than the program's fails the program.

mutants.name: one-module-check-per-package
mutants.rule: The check legs of a program of packages are one ergo check DIR/..., one load of the module, not one per package.

mutants.name: one-module-check-misfiled
mutants.rule: Each envelope of one ergo check DIR/... is judged against its own package's part of the native report, in the order the packages ran.

mutants.name: cache-bound-examples-user-cache
mutants.rule: Every compiler call of the runner builds in the run's own emission cache, which the run removes, never the caller's or the user's.

mutants.name: ex2-no-fix-leg
mutants.rule: A program a clause ergo fix would write fails the examples step (q137).
